record.original_question: Let f₂(n) be the maximum number of edges in a 2-connected graph on n vertices in which no two cycles have the same length. Is it true that lim_{n→∞} (f₂(n) - n)/√n = 1?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.11 ( Boros, Caro, F¨uredi and Yuster [3]) lim f2(n) − n / √n = 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n \geq 3$, let $f_2(n)$ denote the maximum number of edges in a 2-connected simple graph on $n$ vertices having the property that no two distinct cycles have the same length. (A graph is 2-connected if it is connected, has at least 3 vertices, and remains connected after the removal of any single vertex.) Determine whether
$$\lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{f_2(n) - n}{\sqrt{n}} = 1.$$
artifact.category_tag: Extremal graph theory; distinct cycle lengths
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture of Boros, Caro, Füredi and Yuster that (f_2(n)-n)/√n → 1 was resolved by Jie Ma and Tianchi Yang in "Non-repeated cycle lengths and Sidon sequences" (Israel Journal of Mathematics, 2021; arXiv:1808.01548), where they reduce the problem to bounds on Sidon sequences and obtain the matching asymptotic.

status_evidence.title: Non-repeated cycle lengths and Sidon sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Ma and Yang prove the conjecture of Boros, Caro, Füredi and Yuster on the maximum number of edges in a 2-connected graph without repeated cycle lengths.

status_evidence.title: Jie Ma — Non-repeated cycle lengths and Sidon sequences (seminar)
status_evidence.snippet: We prove a conjecture of Boros, Caro, Füredi and Yuster on the maximum number of edges in a 2-connected graph without repeated cycle lengths.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture by BCFY on f_2(n) is proved.

status_evidence.title: Non-repeated cycle lengths and Sidon sequences (preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: Ma–Yang preprint establishing the asymptotic for f_2(n).
status_evidence.claim: Preprint version of the proof of the BCFY conjecture.
